newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - April 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - April 2.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- At least 7,400 members of the Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF) say they are disgruntled with the treatment they are getting from the government and have threatened to defect to the Moro Islamic Liberation Front. Hope of economic improvement have not been realised after the MNLF signed a peace pact with the government. (STAR)
- The Philippines said yesterday it was considering allowing top North Korean defector Hwang Jang-yop to stay in the country for a month. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- The National Bureau of Investigation yesterday began its own autopsy on the body of Filipino geologist Michael de Guzman to unravel the cause of his mysterious death. (TIMES)
- Inflation rate for the month of March is expected to settle around 4.4 percent, the same rate in February, Socioeconomic Planning Secretary Cielito Habito said yesterday. (CHRONICLE/TIMES)

- The U.S. has filed with the World Trade Organisation charges of unfair trade practice against the Philippines over the alleged imposition of restrictions on pork imports, Trade and Industry Secretary Cesar Bautista told reporters yesterday. (STANDARD/INQUIRER)
- The Cabinet yesterday approved the 1997 Investments Priorities Plan, a list of economic activities supported by the government. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
